extracted.intended_audience: patent office policymakers, IP office staff, IP policymakers, and patent/statistics researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting standards for patent office operations, strategic goals, examination quality/timeliness initiatives, international cooperation programs, and conventions for counting and reporting patent filings, applications and grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPO commitment to expeditious and accurate patent examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The JPO is committed to implementing 'expeditious and accurate patent examinations according to the highest global standards' to support an IP-based nation and the intellectual creation cycle of creation, protection and exploitation of IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures described include increasing the number of fixed-term examiners, outsourcing prior art searches to registered private search agencies, establishing a Quality Management system to maintain and improve examination quality, and promoting international cooperation (e.g., PPH and JP-FIRST) to enhance examination performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Management system for patent examinations (JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The JPO has established a Quality Management system intended to maintain and improve the quality of patent examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality management is mentioned alongside staffing increases and outsourcing as part of a combined approach to ensure examination integrity and performance; no scoring rubric provided but presented as an institutional requirement for quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing necessary number of examiners (staffing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Securing the necessary number of examiners through the appointment of new fixed-term examiners is a stated effort to achieve expeditious and efficient examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document cites recruitment targets and year-on-year increases (e.g., expected FY2008 increase of >100 examiners), and shows staffing tables; staffing level is presented as a performance/input metric that reduces examination time and improves throughput.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperless procedures to enable efficiency and outsourcing (JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: JPO established a paperless system for all procedures, from filing to examiner’s decision, enabling outsourcing of prior-art searches to the private sector and significantly enhancing efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report claims this enabled the world’s first outsourcing of prior-art searches and led to JPO processing rates two to four times those of the EPO and USPTO. The paperless system is therefore a procedural standard to improve timeliness and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote international cooperation in patent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote international cooperation through programs such as the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) and JP-FIRST to improve examination efficiency and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International cooperation is framed as a policy instrument to share work, improve timeliness and consistency of examination, and leverage foreign office resources and practices to raise standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy reforms to make IP system more user-friendly (JPO bill amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bill to Partially Amend the Patent Act and Other IP-Related Acts was formulated to establish an IP system more friendly to users and to enable strategic utilization and adequate protection of IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific reforms listed include: revision of the non-exclusive license registration system; revision of the time limit for filing a request for an appeal; expansion of the network of electronic exchange of priority documents; reduction of patent/trademark fees. These items are treated as policy/ procedural changes to improve user experience and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO mission: high quality and timely examination and IP education
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO mission: 'To foster innovation and competitiveness by providing high quality and timely examination of patent and trademark applications, guiding domestic and international intellectual property policy, and delivering intellectual property information and education worldwide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission statement frames the office's performance obligations: deliver high-quality, timely examinations, policy leadership, and dissemination of IP information — these are normative criteria for agency performance and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Strategic Plan goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Strategic Plan (2007-2012) establishes three strategic goals and one management goal: Goal 1: Optimize patent quality and timeliness; Goal 2: Optimize trademark quality and timeliness; Goal 3: Improve intellectual property protection and enforcement domestically and abroad; Management Goal: Achieve organisational excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals are presented as the principal evaluative dimensions for USPTO programs and resource allocation; subsequent practices and metrics are justified by alignment with these goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for strategic planning (USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Strategic Plan was built upon four guiding principles: quality, timeliness, cost-effectiveness, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles function as cross-cutting criteria for designing and assessing programs, investments, and operational changes, and are repeatedly referenced when describing initiatives to improve performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality and timeliness operational measures (USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational measures to optimize patent quality and timeliness include hiring and training large numbers of new examiners, enhanced reviews of allowed patent applications in selected technologies, centralized processing of appeals to ensure compliance with formal requirements, and partnerships with industry to keep examiners’ knowledge current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional systems-level changes include transitioning to an end-to-end, text-based patent prosecution system, increasing remote-work capability with electronic tools for examiners, developing a text-based Patent File Wrapper system to replace image-based systems, and piloting collaboration tools for electronic submission and review. These are concrete procedural standards and capacity-building actions meant to realize the strategic goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark quality and timeliness operational measures (USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures to optimize trademark quality and timeliness include changes in performance plans and incentive awards, increased use of electronic forms (Trademark Electronic Application System Plus), and workflow/process improvements to better manage and track performance and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated as programmatic levers to increase throughput, reduce pendency, and maintain quality in trademark examination, with electronic filing singled out as an efficiency enhancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity-based cost accounting for program transparency (USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO utilizes an activity-based cost accounting methodology to allocate costs across the strategic goals in order to provide transparency to program operational performance and to identify factors driving program costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accounting approach is presented as a standard for fiscal transparency and for informing management decisions and resource allocation tied to strategic objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting conventions for patent statistics (reporting methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different representations of patent filing/processing activity are defined: (a) counts of application forms filled out (direct national, direct regional, PCT international) — each counted once; (b) counts of requests for patents as they entered a grant procedure — direct filings counted once and PCT national/regional phase entries replicated for each procedure started; (c) equivalent numbers of requests for national patent rights — PCT national/regional and direct regional filings replicated over the number of designated countries; (d) patent family counts — sets of first filings counted once each and documented as flows of priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report explains why these representations differ and which figures correspond to which representation (e.g., Fig.3.1 vs Fig.3.5 vs Fig.3.7 vs Fig.3.13). It emphasizes care in interpretation because counting conventions affect trends and cross-office comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and timing rules for PCT national/regional phase counting
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT international-phase applications are treated as subsequent filings; national/regional phase entries are generally considered to begin 30 months after the first filing, which means entry into national/regional phases takes place about 18 months after the PCT international filing for reporting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting numbers for PCT national/regional entries the report replicates PCT applications over the number of procedures they start, which leads to higher counts in grant-procedure statistics compared with raw form-count statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for patent rights metric (expanded-count representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand for patent rights is represented by expanding regional and PCT filings to the number of national patent rights they implicitly request (i.e., replicating regional/PCT filings over member states or designated countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This representation estimates the maximum number of patents that could be obtained from filed applications in a year and shows the effect of centralized procedures on geographical coverage; used to illustrate how international/regional systems allow broader protection with fewer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants counting vs validated national grant registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are counted once each (number of patents granted); validated national grant registrations replicate regional office grants over the number of countries for which the regional grant provides valid registrations, producing a representation in terms of national patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report distinguishes raw grant counts from validated national rights to show the effect of regional granting procedures (e.g., EPO decisions producing multiple national rights).
